mainTopic: Finishing the burial-cave and crowding contradictions of פרק המוכר פירות, then opening the new פרק on selling a בית כור with crevices and rocks
overview: The גמרא has been trying to match the burial-cave measurements in the earlier משנה with the view of רבי שמעון. רב שישא בריה דרב אידי says the משנה does follow רבי שמעון, because one chamber was a smaller one built for נפלים, and that brings the total to twenty אמות. The גמרא asks why both chambers would not be small, which would make eighteen. It answers that we assume only one small chamber, not two. Next the גמרא points out that רבי שמעון and the רבנן seem to switch sides between crowded burials and a crowded vineyard in כלאים. It resolves both contradictions by looking at how people actually behave. Vines are planted to stay, but a farmer will thin out weak ones. A rushed burial may be temporary, and crowded graves are a disgrace. Then פרק המוכר פירות ends, and a new פרק opens with a משנה about selling a בית כור, where wording the sale as exact or as "about" decides whether crevices and rocks of ten טפחים are counted. The גמרא begins by quoting a parallel משנה from ערכין about redeeming a consecrated field, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב שישא: The משנה follows רבי שמעון, with a chamber for נפלים
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי says the משנה really does follow רבי שמעון. It is talking about a case where one chamber was made smaller, for burying נפלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי said: The משנה really does follow רבי שמעון. Here we are dealing with a case of non-viable newborns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the problem of making the משנה's measurements fit רבי שמעון. It says one burial chamber was a small one, made for נפלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A chamber for babies does not need to be full size, so it can be shorter, six אמות. With that smaller chamber, the total length comes out to twenty אמות, which matches the משנה, and we no longer need to say the משנה goes against רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really. It signals that we keep the original assumption after all.
Here, what case are we dealing with? This introduces a specific setting for the text.
Non-viable newborns (נפלים), babies who were not able to live

phrases.aramaic: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said:
Actually, it is Rabbi Shimon,
and here, what are we dealing with? With non-viable newborns.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new answer to the earlier problem of matching the משנה to רבי שמעון
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): one chamber was a small one for נפלים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed not to fit רבי שמעון's measurements
steps.terutzMaskana: With one six-אמה chamber for נפלים, the total is twenty אמות, and the משנה fits רבי שמעון

steps.title: If one chamber is for נפלים, why not the other one too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if one chamber was built small for נפלים, the chamber on the other side could also be small. Then the total would be eighteen, not twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since this chamber is for non-viable newborns, that one is also for non-viable newborns. Then it would come to eighteen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב שישא's answer. If one chamber can be small, why not both?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we allow that a chamber might be built small for babies, there seems to be no reason to stop at just one. Two small chambers plus the courtyard would total only eighteen אמות, which no longer matches the twenty in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And since...
Eighteen
They come to / they amount to

phrases.english: But since this one is for non-viable newborns,
that one is also for non-viable newborns;
they would come to eighteen!
phrases.notes: Six for the small chamber, six for the courtyard, and six for the other small chamber add up to eighteen, not twenty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of רב שישא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שישא's claim that one chamber was for נפלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reasoning would make the second chamber small too, which brings the total to eighteen and breaks the match with the משנה

steps.title: We assume one chamber for נפלים, but not two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is reasonable to assume one chamber was made for נפלים. Assuming two such chambers is not reasonable.
steps.simpleTranslation: We say that one chamber is for non-viable newborns. We do not say that two are for non-viable newborns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב שישא's answer. Only one chamber is assumed to be small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making one chamber small for babies is a reasonable thing to expect. Saying both chambers were made that way would be stretching too far. So the total stays at twenty, and the answer holds.

keyTerms.meaning: One
Two
We say / we assume

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה can follow רבי שמעון: one chamber was a small one for נפלים, and that is how we reach twenty אמות. We assume one such chamber, never two.

phrases.english: One for non-viable newborns, we say;
two for non-viable newborns, we do not say.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא בְּנִיפְלֵי אָמְרִינַן, תַּרְתֵּי בְּנִיפְלֵי לָא אָמְרִינַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the assumption: only one unusual chamber is assumed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If one chamber is small, both might be, which would total eighteen
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one chamber is assumed small, so the total is twenty

steps.title: Contradictions within the רבנן and within רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces a contradiction. The view of the רבנן seems to clash with another ruling of the רבנן, and the same is true for רבי שמעון. This refers to the earlier ברייתא about corpses buried close together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא raises a contradiction between one ruling of the רבנן and another ruling of the רבנן, and between one ruling of רבי שמעון and another ruling of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. It is about to show that both sides seem to contradict themselves, and the source comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier ברייתא about bodies buried close together, the רבנן said this does not count as a graveyard, while רבי שמעון said it can count. The גמרא is about to bring a case where each of them seems to take the opposite position.

keyTerms.meaning: He throws, meaning he raises a contradiction
The Sages (חכמים), the majority opinion
Against (one statement against another)

phrases.english: And he raises a contradiction from the Rabbis against the Rabbis,
and he raises a contradiction from Rabbi Shimon against Rabbi Shimon:
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא quoted earlier, about three bodies buried close together.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָמֵי דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן, וְרָמֵי דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אַדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, going back to the earlier ברייתא about crowded burials
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of the רבנן and רבי שמעון in the ברייתא about crowded burials
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each side seems to take the opposite position in a parallel case of crowding (a vineyard)

steps.title: The source: a crowded vineyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the source of the contradiction. If vines are planted with less than four אמות between them, רבי שמעון says it is not a כרם. The חכמים say it is a כרם, and we treat the middle vines as if they are not there.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: A vineyard planted with less than four אמות between the vines: רבי שמעון says it is not a vineyard. The חכמים say it is a vineyard, and we look at the middle vines as if they are not there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source from הלכות כלאים that creates the contradiction. Here רבי שמעון says crowding cancels the vineyard, and the חכמים say it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With burials, רבי שמעון allowed close-together bodies to count, but here he says close-together vines do not count. The חכמים flip in the opposite direction: they look past the crowded middle vines and still call it a כרם. The גמרא will work out this tension next.

keyTerms.meaning: Vineyard, which matters for the laws of כלאים (mixed planting)
Cubits, a unit of measurement
The middle ones (here, the inner vines)
As if they are not there

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the sides. With burials, the רבנן are the ones who say crowding does NOT count. With vineyards, it is רבי שמעון who says the crowded vineyard does NOT count. That reversal is exactly the contradiction.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: כֶּרֶם הַנָּטוּעַ עַל פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת –
phrases.english: As it is taught: A vineyard that is planted with less than four cubits,
phrases.notes: He means the rows of vines are closer together than four אמות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: It is not a vineyard.
And the Rabbis say: This is a vineyard,
and we view the middle ones as if they are not there.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: כֶּרֶם הַנָּטוּעַ עַל פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the contradiction announced in step 4
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן and רבי שמעון contradict their positions on crowded burials
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in כלאים about a vineyard planted with less than four אמות between the vines

steps.title: Stating the double contradiction
steps.stepSummary: After quoting the vineyard ruling, the גמרא states the problem outright. The רבנן contradict themselves, and so does רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The view of the רבנן is difficult against the other view of the רבנן. And the view of רבי שמעון is difficult against the other view of רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the vineyard source is in front of us, the גמרא states the contradiction clearly. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the burial case, רבי שמעון says we view the middle bodies as if they are not there, and the רבנן do not say this. In the vineyard case, the רבנן say we view the middle vines as if they are not there, and רבי שמעון does not. So each side seems to have switched positions.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; a contradiction or challenge
Against (one ruling set against another)
The Sages, the majority view

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new challenge. It is the same contradiction announced in step 4. The גמרא repeats it now because the vineyard source has been quoted, so the clash is fully clear.

phrases.english: The Rabbis' ruling is difficult against the Rabbis' ruling,
phrases.notes: The burial case is set against the vineyard case. In the vineyard case the רבנן ignore the middle ones, but in the burial case they don't.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon's ruling is difficult against Rabbi Shimon's ruling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the quoted vineyard ruling and states the contradiction it creates.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of both רבי שמעון and the רבנן across the burial and vineyard rulings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each side treats the middle items as not there in one case but not in the other, so each seems inconsistent.

steps.title: Why רבי שמעון treats vines and graves differently
steps.stepSummary: People plant vines to keep them, so the middle vines are real. But a body is sometimes buried in a rush right before שבת, planning to move it later. So in graves the middle ones can be ignored.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction within רבי שמעון's views is not difficult. There, in the vineyard, people do not plant vines planning to uproot them. Here, in burial, sometimes a death happens right at בין השמשות before שבת, and people put the body down wherever there is room.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first half of the contradiction, the one about רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vines are planted to stay, so every vine counts and the middle vines cannot be ignored. A body buried in a hurry at בין השמשות is only a temporary burial, meant to be moved later. That is why רבי שמעון can treat the middle bodies as if they are not there.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
With the intention of uprooting
Twilight, here the last moments before שבת begins
Happens to place, puts down casually

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אַדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא קַשְׁיָא –
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon against Rabbi Shimon is not difficult –

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, לָא נָטְעִי אִינָשֵׁי אַדַּעְתָּא לְמִיעְקַר;
phrases.english: there, people do not plant with the intention of uprooting;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, זִימְנִין דְּמִיתְרְמֵא לֵיהּ בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת,
phrases.english: here, sometimes it happens to him at twilight,
phrases.notes: "Here" means burial. Someone dies right before שבת, and there's no time for a proper burial.

phrases.english: and they place him down wherever it happens.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אַדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבי שמעון half of the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the person's intention (permanent versus temporary)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון seemed to apply opposite rules to two cases of crowded items.
steps.terutzMaskana: Vines are planted to stay, so they all count. A rushed burial is temporary, so the middle bodies can be ignored.

steps.title: Why the רבנן treat graves and vines differently
steps.stepSummary: Graves packed too closely are a disgrace and do not count as real graves. But a farmer is happy for weak vines to be removed, so the middle vines can be ignored.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction within the רבנן's views is also not difficult. Here, in burial, since crowding is a disgrace, it is not called a grave. There, in the vineyard, the owner says: whichever vines grow well, let them grow, and whichever do not grow well can be used for firewood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second half of the contradiction, the one about the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burying bodies crammed together is disrespectful, so such a spot is not considered a proper grave area. The middle bodies are not ignored to make it count. With vines, the owner expects to uproot the weak ones, so the רבנן view the middle vines as if they are already gone.

keyTerms.meaning: It is disgraceful
Grave
Good, flourishing
Firewood

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides are consistent, and each one looks at how real people treat crowded vines and crowded graves. רבי שמעון: vines are planted to stay, so the middle vines count, but a rushed burial may be temporary, so the middle bodies can be ignored. רבנן: crowded graves are a disgrace and do not count as graves, but a farmer is willing to thin out weak vines, so the middle vines are ignored.

phrases.english: The Rabbis against the Rabbis is also not difficult –

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּמִינַּוַּל – לָא מִקְּרֵי קֶבֶר;
phrases.english: here, since it is disgraceful, it is not called a grave;
there, he says to himself:
phrases.notes: "He" is the owner of the vineyard.

phrases.english: whichever of them does well, does well,
and whichever does not do well, let it be for firewood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן half of the contradiction, which completes the resolution.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by how people view them (disgrace versus willingness to thin out)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן seemed to ignore the middle items in one case but not in the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Crowded graves are a disgrace and do not count as graves. Crowded vines are expected to be thinned, so the middle ones are ignored.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק המוכר פירות
steps.stepSummary: The פרק of המוכר פירות ends with the traditional closing line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק המוכר פירות.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line said at the end of a פרק. The discussion of this chapter is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן marks the end of the sixth פרק of בבא בתרא. The next פרק will open with a new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the closing formula of a פרק
"One who sells produce", the name of this פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, "One who sells produce"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final contradiction is resolved.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק המוכר פירות is complete.

steps.title: Selling an exact בית כור: big crevices and rocks are not counted
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that when someone sells an exact בית כור of land, crevices ten טפחים deep or rocks ten טפחים high are not counted in the measurement. Smaller ones are counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone tells his friend, "I am selling you a בית כור of soil," and the field has crevices ten טפחים deep or rocks ten טפחים high, those spots are not counted as part of the measurement. If they are smaller than that, they are counted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה about measuring land that was sold by a set size. It explains which parts of the field count toward the size the buyer paid for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer was promised a full בית כור of usable soil. A crevice or rock of ten טפחים is treated as a separate area, not ordinary field, so it does not count toward his land. Anything smaller is just part of a normal field and is included.

keyTerms.meaning: An area of land big enough to plant a כור of seed
Crevices or hollows in the ground
Rocks
Handbreadths, a unit of measurement
They are measured together with it, counted as part of the field

steps.whyThisMatters: Ten טפחים is the measure that turns a dip or a rock into its own separate area. This idea is the base for the rest of the sugya.

phrases.english: One who says to his fellow:
"I am selling you a beit kor of soil" –
phrases.notes: A בית כור is a fixed size of field, the area where you would plant a כור of seed.

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ שָׁם נְקָעִים עֲמוּקִּים עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.english: if there were crevices there ten handbreadths deep,
or rocks ten handbreadths high –
they are not measured with it.
phrases.notes: He means they don't count toward the בית כור; the seller has to give other land to make up the size.

phrases.english: Less than this, they are measured with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ: ״בֵּית כּוֹר עָפָר אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לָךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the new פרק right after the הדרן closing פרק המוכר פירות in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In an exact sale of a בית כור, crevices or rocks of ten טפחים are not counted toward the measurement; smaller ones are.

steps.title: Selling about a בית כור: even big crevices and rocks are counted
steps.stepSummary: If the seller said "about a בית כור," even crevices deeper than ten טפחים or rocks higher than ten טפחים are counted in the measurement.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the seller said, "about a בית כור of soil," then even crevices more than ten טפחים deep, or rocks more than ten טפחים high, are counted as part of the field.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second half of its rule. Changing the wording to "about" changes what gets counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra letter כ ("like" or "about") shows the seller was only giving a rough size. So the buyer cannot be strict about the measurement, and even the big crevices and rocks are included.

keyTerms.meaning: About a בית כור, a rough size and not exact
More than ten

steps.whatToRemember: Exact wording ("a בית כור") means big crevices and rocks of ten טפחים are not counted. Loose wording ("about a בית כור") means even bigger ones are counted.
steps.confusionAlert: The whole difference between the two cases is one small letter, the כ in כבית כור. Don't read past it.

phrases.english: And if he said to him: "about a beit kor of soil" –
even if there were crevices there, deep
more than ten handbreadths,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ סְלָעִים גְּבוֹהִין יוֹתֵר מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.english: or rocks higher than ten handbreadths,
these are measured with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to step 10: the seller used loose wording instead of an exact size.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the sale is of "about a בית כור," even crevices or rocks of more than ten טפחים are counted in the measurement.

steps.title: The גמרא brings a parallel משנה about a consecrated field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from ערכין: someone who consecrates his field during the time of the יובל redeems it at fifty silver שקלים for each area where a חומר of barley is sown. It then starts to ask what happens if the field has crevices or rocks of ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in another משנה: a person who consecrates his field when the יובל is in force pays fifty silver שקלים for every area big enough to sow a חומר of barley. If the field had crevices ten טפחים deep or rocks ten טפחים high...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by quoting a similar case from a different משנה. The quote stops in the middle, and the ruling about the crevices and rocks continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both משניות deal with measuring a field that has deep crevices or tall rocks. By bringing the case of a consecrated field, the גמרא is getting ready to compare how those spots are treated there with how they are treated in a sale.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
One who consecrates something to the בית המקדש
The Jubilee year, every fiftieth year
A חומר of barley, the same size as a כור
A silver coin

phrases.english: GEMARA:
We learned there:
phrases.notes: "There" means a משנה in a different place, in ערכין.

phrases.english: One who consecrates his field at the time of the Jubilee,

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתֵן לוֹ לְבֵית זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים –
phrases.english: he gives, for each area for sowing a chomer of barley,
fifty silver shekels.

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ שָׁם נְקָעִים עֲמוּקִּים עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.english: If there were crevices there ten handbreadths deep,
or rocks ten handbreadths high –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the new משנה by bringing a parallel source about measuring a field with crevices and rocks.
steps.raayaObject: How crevices and rocks of ten טפחים are treated when a field is measured, as in the משנה of the sale.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in ערכין about redeeming a consecrated field at fifty silver שקלים per בית זרע חומר שעורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who consecrates his field during the time of the יובל redeems it at fifty silver שקלים for each בית זרע חומר שעורים. The ruling on crevices and rocks of ten טפחים is cut off at the end of this amud.
